3. The Defendant No.1 contested the suit by filing a written statement denying the material allegation to the plaint and asserted that since the plaintiff did not repay the mortgage money amounting to Tk. 1500/- he is not entitled to get any decree in the suit. 

 4. The defendant No. 2 and 3 filed a joint written statement stating inter alia that the defendant No. 1 purchased the suit land from the plaintiff and while possessing the same R.S. record was prepared in his name and on requirement of money the defendant No.1 transferred 21 decimals of land in favour of the defendant No.2 and 3 by a registered kabala No. 1953/87 dated 18.3.1987 and delivered possession thereof in favour of them and since they were possessing the same and as such the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

 that the trans action was out and out Usufructury Mortgage and after lapse of 7 years, the defendant No. 1 was bound to reconvey the land free from encumbrance under section 95A of the state Acquisition and Tenancy Act, That being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and decree of the trial court the defendants preferred an appeal before the learned District Judge and on transfer it was heard and disposed of by the learned subordinate Judge, Artha Rin Adalat, Rajshahi who has' allowed the appeal by setting aside the judgment of the trial court in relying a decision reported in 3 B. L. T. 141 (AD) holding that the plaintiff is not entitled to get any decree as per section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. 

 7. Mr. Munsur Habib the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the plaintiff-petitioner submits that the learned court of appeal below. has misconstrued section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, Section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act reads as follows : 

 a complete usufrucuary mortgage for a period not exceeding seven years and the provisions of section 95 shall apply to such transfer whether made before or after the date of commencement of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. 

 9. Mr. Waziullah alOngwith Mrs. Amatul Karim the learned advocates appearing on behalf of the opposite party could not substantiate their argument in view of section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. 

 10. Since the petitioner invokes Section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act that after enjoyment of the usufruct for maximum period of 7 years he is entitled to get back his property and the suit having been filed on 20.5.1990. is within the period of limitation. Therefore, the cited . decision reported in 3 B.L.T. (AD) 141 has got no application in this particular case as the transaction is construed to be a mortgage for a period of 7 years. The transaction was alive and subsisting on the date of promulgation of P.0.88 of 1972 i.e. on 3.8.72.
